name: Amaranth Deep Purple
lede: Amaranth Deep Purple is a dark magenta-pink from the Maerz and Paul color dictionary, naming a purplish-red that borrows its first word from the amaranth flower family of color names.

sections.title: From a dye-plant's family of names
sections.body:
ColorHub's library notes that this name is cited by Wikipedia back to Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary, placing it in our standard-reference tier alongside other dictionary and ISCC-NBS names rather than in the everyday or nature lists [1]. The nearest named colors on file are [[traffic-purple]], [[maximum-red-purple]], [[dark-fuchsia]] and [[flirt]], at 4, 4.2, 4.2 and 4.3 ΔE [1]. The hex #9F2B68 measures a vivid purplish red by ISCC-NBS, 6.9 units from its nearest block, close to 5.3RP 3.8/11.5 in Munsell notation [2].

Its closest listed library neighbor is [[plum]], 9.0 units away, which places it nearer to a true purple-red than to the brighter, pinker end of the amaranth family [2]. [[maroon]] sits just to the browner side of the same dark red-purple range [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Amaranth Deep Purple in only 3 of 23,781 paintings, 0.01 percent, making it rarer than about 79 percent of the named colors we track [3]. Every one of the three dated matches comes from a single year, 1900, which is too small a sample to draw any century-level trend from, so we report it as a bare count rather than a lift [3]. All matches are computed against photographs of varnished, aged canvases, not pigment identifications [3]. These are photographs of aged, varnished paintings, read as screen colors, not pigment identifications[3].
